title: Napoleonic Code (French Civil Code)
summary: On 21 March 1804 (30 Ventôse an XII), a law under First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte united 36 separately passed laws into the Code civil des Français. It drew on the Roman written law of southern France and the customary law of the north. It freed property from feudal burdens and protected private property, though equality was not absolute: wives and foreigners did not have equal civil rights. It was adopted across much of continental Europe and used as a model in many Latin American countries.

uncertainty.note: Promulgated as a single unified code on 30 Ventôse an XII (21 March 1804); 36 individual titles were debated and enacted between March 1803 and March 1804.

as_recorded.value: 21 Mar 1804 The Code Napoleon is officially adopted as the French Civil Code, laying the foundation for French civil law , including religious freedoms and property rights, observed today.
The law of 30 ventôse, an XII united the thirty-six sections passed by the legislature into the name "Code civil des Français".
Le Code civil des Français, 21 mars 1804

importance.justification: Replaced France's divided legal systems with one civil code that was widely adopted and imitated abroad.

related.because: The French Revolution abolished feudal legal privileges and established the requirement for a uniform national civil code.
